9289.t: Has been derived from Proto-Indo-European *terkʷ-, with cognates including Sanskrit तर्कु (tarku), Albanian dredh and Latin torqueō.

9273.t: Unclear. Has been derived from ἄρκυς (ắrkŭs, “net”).

9238.t: From the adjective ἁγνός (hagnós, “chaste”), unless this is a folk etymology which led to the cultural associations with chastity, rather than the reverse.

9272.t: Probably from Proto-Indo-European *h₂éristos (“fittest, most fitting, most suitable”), the superlative of *h₂er- (“to fit, be suitable”).

9233.t: From ἁ- (hă-, “one, same”) + -πλόος (-plóos, “-fold”). Compare διπλόος (dĭplóos, “double”), as well as Latin simplex.

9251.t: The etymology continues to be debated.

9299.t: From ἅλλομαι (hắllomai, “to jump, to leap”) and the suffix -μα (-ma).

9279.t: Unknown. Clearly related to some names of coltsfoot given by 1st century interpolations to Dioskurides, ἀσᾶ (asâ) with the Thracians of Βῆσσα, σααρθρά (saarthrá) with the Egyptians.

9270.t: According to Beekes, of Pre-Greek origin.

9237.t: From Proto-Indo-European *m̥ǵ-éh₂-m, accusative singular of *méǵh₂s (“great”, whence μέγας (mégăs)).

9269.t: The formation is similar to κέλαδος (kélados) and ὅμαδος (hómados). Perhaps onomatopoeic but compare ἄραβος (árabos).

9208.t: According to Beekes, the connection with ἀφιέναι (aphiénai, “flowers”) proposed by Theophrastus is unsustainable.

9287.t: From Proto-Indo-European *sn̥Hter (whence also Proto-Germanic *sunder (“apart; separately”)), from *senH-; cognate with ἄνευ (ắneu), as well as Latin sine and Sanskrit स॒नि॒तुर् (sanitúr)).

9284.t: Verbal adjective of ἀ- (ă-, “not”) + σῴζω (sōízō, “to save”).

9206.t: According to Beekes, of Pre-Greek origin, in view of the suffix -βος.

9285.t: From ἀ- (a-, “not, without”) + τάσσω (tássō, “draw up in order of battle, form, array, marshal”) + -τος (-tos, adjectival suffix).

9271.t: Furnée compares παρδακός (pardakós, “humid”) (highly doubtful) and ἄρσεα (ársea, “humid meadows”). The latter proposal is attractive, as -σος is a typical Pre-Greek suffix.

9275.t: From ἀ- (a-) + ῥήγνυμι (rhḗgnūmi, “to break, shatter”) + -τος (-tos, adjective suffix).

9201.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *né Proto-Indo-European *n̥- Proto-Hellenic *ə- Ancient Greek ἀ- (a-) Proto-Indo-European *kʷelh₁- Proto-Hellenic *kʷélos Ancient Greek τέλος (télos) Proto-Indo-European *-is Proto-Indo-European *-h₂ Proto-Indo-European…

9282.t: From ἀ- (ă-) + the root of ἵστημι (hĭ́stēmĭ) + -τος (-tos)

9229.t: Denominal verb of ἁλιεύς (halieús, “fisher”); also analyzable as ἅλς (háls, “saltwater, seawater”) + -εύω (-eúō).

9298.t: Possibly from Proto-Indo-European *seh₂- (“satiate; satisfy”) + -δην (-dēn, adverbial suffix). If so, cognate with Gothic 𐍃𐌰𐌸𐍃 (saþs).

9274.t: * The first sense is usually compared with ἄρνυμαι (árnumai, “to gain, win”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₂er- (“to acquire, take”), * the second sense has been compared with Laconian/Tsakonian ἀρέ (aré, “cistern”), but this word is obscure. *…
